raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation On MI350X / MI355X (gfx950), Kimi-K3 KDA decode runs the unfused chain by default (`f_b` tiny GEMM, causal Conv1D update, Triton recurrent decode, gated RMSNorm), or the AITER FlyDSL fused boundary with `SGLANG_ROCM_K3_KDA_FUSED_BACKEND=aiter`. This PR adds a HIP kernel for the same fused boundary and makes it the default on gfx950. It is the decode companion of #45710 (KDA prefill); the two PRs change disjoint runtime files. **Note: This kernel is generated by [KDAgent](https://nvlabs.github.io/kda/blog/2026-09-27-kda-for-kda/) in AMD ecosystems. Cost around 5k dollars in humanize2 flow to get this.** ## Modifications The kernel follows the `sglang.kernels` layout of RFC #29630: it was produced with the Kernel Design Agents workflow, so the implementation lives in `kernels/kda_kernels`, it is registered with `KernelBackend.KDA`, and runtime code reaches it only through the `sglang.kernels.ops` facade. - `kernels/kda_kernels/csrc/attention/kda_decode_gfx950.cu` and its loader `kernels/kda_kernels/kda_decode_gfx950.py`, JIT-compiled on first use. One 256-thread workgroup per (token, head), for 12 heads of 128 per rank (Kimi-K3 TP8), runs the `f_b` projection, the depthwise Conv1D update with SiLU, the q/k L2 norms and gate decay, the delta-rule update of the 128 x 128 fp32 state, and the gated RMSNorm. State and Conv1D slot strides are read from the tensors, so padded hybrid cache layouts work. Slot 0, the mamba pool's padding slot, returns zeros without touching either cache. - `kernels/kda_kernels/README.md`: provenance entry. - `kernels/ops/attention/__init__.py`: registers `attention.kda_decode_gfx950` (`KernelBackend.KDA`, HIP). - `kernels/ops/attention/kda_fused_decode_gfx950.py` (facade): the same fail-closed `available` / `covered` / `warmup` / `run` interface as `kda_fused_decode_aiter_hip`; `run` calls the kernel through `get_kernel`. - `srt/models/kimi_k3.py` (ROCm branch of `_prepare_fused_decode`): maps `SGLANG_ROCM_K3_KDA_FUSED_BACKEND` to a facade, `gfx950` (the new default) or `aiter`; any other value keeps the unfused chain. The chosen facade is stored on the layer. - `srt/layers/attention/linear/kda_backend.py` (gfx950 fused-decode branch): calls the facade stored on the layer instead of the hard-coded AITER adapter. - `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_kda_fused_decode_gfx950.py` (MI35x suite): matches the Triton chain over 4 steps under the default backend, skips slots <= 0, and CUDA graph replay equals eager. Behavior change: on gfx950 the fused decode is now on by default. `SGLANG_ROCM_K3_KDA_FUSED_BACKEND=aiter` selects FlyDSL, and any other value (for example `none`) selects the unfused chain. Both edits in `srt/` are inside the existing ROCm-only branches. ## Accuracy Tests MI355X, `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.22-rocm10-mi35x-20261020`. - Against a per-token fp32 PyTorch reference (batch 1, 2, 8 and 37 with padded rows, and batch 16 over 64 steps): output relative RMSE at most 7.1e-6 (the Triton chain reaches 1.2e-5 and FlyDSL 2.7e-5 in the same checks). The Conv1D state is bit-identical; padded rows return zeros and slot 0 is untouched. - Pass: the new test, `unit/kernels/test_kernels_namespace.py` (includes the KDA directory/backend pairing check), `kernels/ops/attention/kda_flydsl/test_kimi_k3_kda_decode.py`, `attention/unittests/kda/test_triton.py`, `attention/test_kda_kernels.py`, `kernels/ops/attention/test_fused_kda_conv_recurrent_verify.py` and `amd/test_kimi_k3_kda_inproj_fusion.py`. - Kimi-K3 TP8 GSM8K (8-shot, 1319 questions): 0.960 with both HIP kernels off, 0.961 with this PR and #45710 on. ## Speed Tests and Profiling **Kernel.** Per-layer time inside a 69-layer CUDA graph with a separate cache per layer (median of 11 trials): | Batch | Triton chain | FlyDSL | HIP | vs Triton chain | vs FlyDSL | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | 11.51 us | 8.54 us | 5.96 us | 1.93x | 1.43x | | 2 | 11.60 us | 8.45 us | 6.09 us | 1.90x | 1.39x | | 4 | 13.45 us | 10.44 us | 7.15 us | 1.88x | 1.46x | | 8 | 27.42 us | 11.82 us | 7.93 us | 3.46x | 1.49x | | 16 | 29.87 us | 13.92 us | 9.91 us | 3.02x | 1.41x | | 32 | 33.60 us | 19.65 us | 16.21 us | 2.07x | 1.21x | | 64 | 38.26 us | 31.50 us | 26.28 us | 1.46x | 1.20x | | 128 | 61.11 us | 56.29 us | 46.68 us | 1.31x | 1.21x | | 256 | 108.86 us | 100.83 us | 86.48 us | 1.26x | 1.17x | For reference, AITER's Triton/Gluon packed KDA decode (not a SGLang backend) is 1.10x-1.30x slower than HIP up to batch 32 and 3%-6% faster from batch 64. **The model runs the kernel.** Kimi-K3 TP8, rank-0 GPU profile (`/start_profile`) of one 10,244-token request with 8 output tokens (7 decode steps x 69 KDA layers = 483 layer steps): | Kernels (calls) | Baseline | This PR + #45710 | |---|---|---| | KDA decode | `_causal_conv1d_update_kernel` (483), `fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update_kernel` (483), `layer_norm_gated_fwd_kernel` (483 of 552) | `kda_decode_gfx950_kernel` (483); none of the three | **Kimi-K3 TP8 E2E.** Measured with this PR and #45710 applied; the baseline sets `SGLANG_ROCM_KDA_HIP_PREFILL=0 SGLANG_ROCM_K3_KDA_FUSED_BACKEND=none`, which is the current `main` behavior. Baseline and candidate servers were launched alternately, two rounds each; the table shows the mean of the two rounds. ```bash SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 SGLANG_AITER_K3_OPT=1 AITER_FLYDSL_FORCE=1 AITER_SITUV2_A8W4=1 \ python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path moonshotai/Kimi-K3 --tp-size 8 \ --attention-backend triton --dtype bfloat16 --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \ --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 64 --max-running-requests 64 \ --reasoning-parser kimi_k3 --tool-call-parser kimi_k3 --trust-remote-code python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang --dataset-name random-ids \ --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 512 --random-range-ratio 1 \ --num-prompts 80 --max-concurrency 16 --warmup-requests 16 --flush-cache --seed 42 # also: --num-prompts 320 --max-concurrency 64; and --random-input-len 8192 # --random-output-len 64 --num-prompts 40 --max-concurrency 8 --warmup-requests 8 python3 -m sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k --num-shots 8 --num-questions 1319 \ --max-new-tokens 512 --parallel 64 ``` | Workload | Metric | Baseline | Both PRs | Change | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1024 in / 512 out, concurrency 16 | median TPOT | 23.7 ms | 22.9 ms | -3.6% | | | median ITL | 23.8 ms | 22.9 ms | -3.8% | | | output throughput | 617.7 tok/s | 642.7 tok/s | +4.1% | | 1024 in / 512 out, concurrency 64 | median TPOT | 33.5 ms | 32.4 ms | -3.2% | | | median ITL | 33.5 ms | 32.5 ms | -2.9% | | | output throughput | 1536.7 tok/s | 1590.1 tok/s | +3.5% | | 8192 in / 64 out, concurrency 8 | median TPOT | 20.2 ms | 19.5 ms | -3.8% | | | median ITL | 20.6 ms | 19.8 ms | -3.8% | | | output throughput | 99.5 tok/s | 102.4 tok/s | +3.0% | The two rounds of each server differed by at most 0.6% in output throughput.
Decode throughput with bench_one_batch_server `steady_state_output_throughput` of `python3 -m sglang.bench_one_batch_server --model None --base-url http://127.0.0.1:30000 --batch-size 1 8 32 64 --input-len 1024 --output-len 512 --dataset-name random-ids`, median of 2 runs; the steady-state window excludes prefill: | Batch | Baseline | This PR | Change | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | 69.2 tok/s | 72.4 tok/s | +4.6% | | 8 | 378.1 tok/s | 385.4 tok/s | +1.9% | | 32 | 1137.2 tok/s | 1174.1 tok/s | +3.2% | | 64 | 1779.7 tok/s | 1866.6 tok/s | +4.9% |
The Kimi-K3 cookbook's MI355X recipe (DCP8, AITER attention, fp8 KV cache) failed to allocate the KDA state cache on this image for both variants, so these runs use Triton attention without DCP. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). (isort, ruff, ruff-format, codespell, clang-format) - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (`kda_kernels/README.md` provenance entry added; the Kimi-K3 cookbook's "Fused KDA Decode (AMD gfx950)" toggle still lists only `aiter`.) - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #39713408703](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39713408703) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #39713408519](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39713408519) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :x: [Run #39713408648](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39713408648)

@@ -0,0 +1,82 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+"""HIP Kimi-K3 fused Kimi Delta Attention decode for gfx950 (MI350X / MI355X).
+
+The extension is JIT-compiled with ``torch.utils.cpp_extension`` on first use
+and cached under ``TORCH_EXTENSIONS_DIR``.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import os
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.kernels.kda_kernels import _cuda_source
+
+_ext = None
+
+
+def load_ext():
+    """Build and cache the gfx950 HIP extension."""
+    global _ext
+    if _ext is None:
+        from sglang.srt.utils.cpp_extension_loader import (
+            load_extension_with_recovery,
+        )
+

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+"""HIP Kimi-K3 fused KDA decode for gfx950 (MI350X / MI355X).
+
+Same fail-closed interface as ``kda_fused_decode_aiter_hip``: it serves
+``SGLANG_ROCM_K3_KDA_FUSED_BACKEND=gfx950`` (the default on ROCm), and inputs it
+does not cover keep the unfused KDA decode. The kernel is
+``attention.kda_decode_gfx950`` (``KernelBackend.KDA``), implemented in
+``sglang.kernels.kda_kernels.kda_decode_gfx950``.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import os
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.kernels.selector import get_kernel
+from sglang.kernels.spec import KernelBackend
+from sglang.srt.utils import is_hip
+
+_HEADS = 12
+_DIM = 128
+_CHANNELS = 3 * _HEADS * _DIM
+
+
+def enabled() -> bool:
+    backend = os.environ.get("SGLANG_ROCM_K3_KDA_FUSED_BACKEND", "gfx950")
+    return backend.lower() == "gfx950"
+
+
+def available(device: torch.device | None = None) -> bool:
+    if not is_hip() or not enabled() or not torch.cuda.is_available():
+        return False
+    arch = torch.cuda.get_device_properties(device).gcnArchName
+    return arch.split(":", 1)[0] == "gfx950"
+
+
+def warmup(**_: object) -> None:
+    from sglang.kernels.kda_kernels.kda_decode_gfx950 import load_ext
+
+    load_ext()
+
+
+def covered(
+    f_a: torch.Tensor,
+    f_b_weight: torch.Tensor,
+    mixed_qkv: torch.Tensor,
+    raw_beta: torch.Tensor,
+    conv_state: torch.Tensor,
+    state: torch.Tensor,
+    state_indices: torch.Tensor,
+    output_gate: torch.Tensor,
+    norm_weight: torch.Tensor,
+) -> bool:
+    if not available(f_a.device) or f_a.ndim != 2:
+        return False
+    batch = f_a.shape[0]
+    return (
+        batch > 0
+        and f_a.shape == (batch, _DIM)
+        and f_a.dtype == torch.bfloat16
+        and f_a.stride(-1) == 1
+        and f_b_weight.shape == (_HEADS, _DIM, _DIM)
+        and f_b_weight.dtype == torch.bfloat16
+        and f_b_weight.is_contiguous()
+        and mixed_qkv.shape == (batch, _CHANNELS)
+        and mixed_qkv.dtype == torch.bfloat16
+        and mixed_qkv.stride(-1) == 1
+        and raw_beta.shape == (1, batch, _HEADS)
+        and raw_beta.dtype == torch.bfloat16
+        and raw_beta.stride(-1) == 1
+        and conv_state.ndim == 3
+        and conv_state.shape[1:] == (_CHANNELS, 3)
+        and conv_state.dtype == torch.bfloat16
+        and state.ndim == 4
+        and state.shape[1:] == (_HEADS, _DIM, _DIM)
+        and state.dtype == torch.float32
+        and state.stride()[-3:] == (_DIM * _DIM, _DIM, 1)
+        and state_indices.shape == (batch,)
+        and state_indices.dtype == torch.int32
+        and state_indices.stride(0) == 1
+        and output_gate.shape == (batch, _HEADS, _DIM)
+        and output_gate.dtype == torch.bfloat16
+        and output_gate.stride()[-2:] == (_DIM, 1)
+        and norm_weight.shape == (_DIM,)
+        and norm_weight.dtype == torch.bfloat16
+        and norm_weight.is_contiguous()
+    )
+
+
+def run(
+    *,
+    f_a: torch.Tensor,
+    f_b_weight: torch.Tensor,
+    mixed_qkv: torch.Tensor,
+    conv_weight: torch.Tensor,
+    conv_state: torch.Tensor,
+    raw_beta: torch.Tensor,
+    A_log: torch.Tensor,
+    dt_bias: torch.Tensor,
+    lower_bound: float,
+    state: torch.Tensor,
+    state_indices: torch.Tensor,
+    output_gate: torch.Tensor,
+    norm_weight: torch.Tensor,
+    norm_eps: float,
+    out: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    if out is None:
+        out = f_a.new_empty((1, f_a.shape[0], _HEADS, _DIM))
+    get_kernel("attention.kda_decode_gfx950", KernelBackend.KDA)(
+        f_a,
+        f_b_weight,
+        mixed_qkv,
+        conv_weight.contiguous(),
+        conv_state,
+        raw_beta,
+        A_log,
+        dt_bias,
+        state,
+        state_indices,
+        output_gate,
+        norm_weight,
+        out,
+        lower_bound,
+        norm_eps,
+    )
+    return out

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+
+import os
+import unittest
+from unittest.mock import patch
+
+import torch
+import torch.nn.functional as F
+
+from sglang.kernels.ops.attention import kda_fused_decode_gfx950
+from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.fla.fused_norm_gate import FusedRMSNormGated
+from sglang.kernels.ops.mamba.causal_conv1d_triton import causal_conv1d_update
+from sglang.srt.layers.attention.linear.kernels.kda_triton import TritonKDAKernel
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_amd_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_amd_ci(est_time=120, suite="stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x")
+
+H, D = 12, 128
+C = 3 * H * D
+LOWER_BOUND = -5.0
+NORM_EPS = 1e-5
+
+
+def _is_gfx950() -> bool:
+    return bool(
+        torch.version.hip
+        and torch.cuda.is_available()
+        and torch.cuda.get_device_properties().gcnArchName.split(":", 1)[0] == "gfx950"
+    )
+
+
+def _inputs(indices, slots=8) -> dict[str, torch.Tensor]:
+    batch = len(indices)
+    generator = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(batch)
+
+    def randn(shape, scale=1.0, dtype=torch.bfloat16):
+        return (torch.randn(shape, generator=generator, device="cuda") * scale).to(
+            dtype
+        )
+
+    # The model slices these from one projection; an odd row width leaves
+    # the slices unaligned.
+    fused = randn((batch, C + H * D + D + H + 1))
+    return {
+        "mixed_qkv": fused[:, :C],
+        "output_gate": fused[:, C : C + H * D].view(batch, H, D),
+        "f_a": fused[:, C + H * D : C + H * D + D],
+        "raw_beta": fused[:, C + H * D + D : C + H * D + D + H].unsqueeze(0),
+        "f_b_weight": randn((H, D, D), 0.05),
+        "conv_weight": randn((C, 4), 0.3, torch.float32),
+        "conv_state": randn((slots, 3, C)).transpose(-1, -2),
+        "A_log": randn((H,), 0.5, torch.float32),
+        "dt_bias": randn((H * D,), 0.1, torch.float32),
+        "state": randn((slots, H, D, D), 0.05, torch.float32),
+        "state_indices": torch.tensor(indices, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32),
+        "norm_weight": randn((D,)),
+    }
+
+
+def _clone_caches(inputs):
+    cloned = dict(inputs)
+    cloned["conv_state"] = inputs["conv_state"].transpose(-1, -2).clone()
+    cloned["conv_state"] = cloned["conv_state"].transpose(-1, -2)
+    cloned["state"] = inputs["state"].clone()
+    return cloned
+
+
+def _triton_chain(inputs):
+    gate = F.linear(inputs["f_a"], inputs["f_b_weight"].view(H * D, D))
+    qkv = causal_conv1d_update(
+        inputs["mixed_qkv"],
+        inputs["conv_state"],
+        inputs["conv_weight"],
+        None,
+        activation="silu",
+        conv_state_indices=inputs["state_indices"],
+    )
+    out = TritonKDAKernel().packed_decode(
+        qkv,
+        gate,
+        inputs["raw_beta"],
+        A_log=inputs["A_log"],
+        dt_bias=inputs["dt_bias"],
+        scale=D**-0.5,
+        ssm_states=inputs["state"],
+        cache_indices=inputs["state_indices"],
+        num_v_heads=H,
+        head_v_dim=D,
+        lower_bound=LOWER_BOUND,
+    )
+    norm = FusedRMSNormGated(D, eps=NORM_EPS, activation="sigmoid").cuda()
+    norm.weight.data = inputs["norm_weight"]
+    return norm(out, inputs["output_gate"])
+
+
+def _fused(inputs, out=None):
+    return kda_fused_decode_gfx950.run(
+        lower_bound=LOWER_BOUND, norm_eps=NORM_EPS, out=out, **inputs
+    )
+
+
+@unittest.skipUnless(_is_gfx950(), "gfx950 KDA decode requires MI35x")
+class TestGfx950KDAFusedDecode(CustomTestCase):
+    @torch.inference_mode()
+    def test_matches_triton_chain_over_steps(self):
+        inputs = _inputs([3, 1, -1, 6, 5])
+        expected_inputs = _clone_caches(inputs)
+        actual_inputs = _clone_caches(inputs)
+        # the default backend
+        with patch.dict(os.environ):
+            os.environ.pop("SGLANG_ROCM_K3_KDA_FUSED_BACKEND", None)
+            self.assertTrue(
+                kda_fused_decode_gfx950.covered(
+                    *(
+                        inputs[name]
+                        for name in (
+                            "f_a",
+                            "f_b_weight",
+                            "mixed_qkv",
+                            "raw_beta",
+                            "conv_state",
+                            "state",
+                            "state_indices",
+                            "output_gate",
+                            "norm_weight",
+                        )
+                    )
+                )
+            )
+        for _ in range(4):
+            expected = _triton_chain(expected_inputs)
+            actual = _fused(actual_inputs)
+            torch.testing.assert_close(
+                actual.float(), expected.float(), rtol=1e-2, atol=1e-2
+            )
+        torch.testing.assert_close(
+            actual_inputs["state"], expected_inputs["state"], rtol=1e-4, atol=1e-4
+        )
+        self.assertTrue(
+            torch.equal(actual_inputs["conv_state"], expected_inputs["conv_state"])
+        )
+
+    @torch.inference_mode()
+    def test_non_positive_slots_are_skipped(self):
+        inputs = _inputs([0, -1, 4])
+        actual_inputs = _clone_caches(inputs)
+        actual = _fused(actual_inputs)
+        self.assertEqual(torch.count_nonzero(actual[:, :2]).item(), 0)
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(actual_inputs["state"][0], inputs["state"][0]))
+        self.assertTrue(
+            torch.equal(actual_inputs["conv_state"][0], inputs["conv_state"][0])
+        )
+        self.assertFalse(torch.equal(actual_inputs["state"][4], inputs["state"][4]))
+
+    @torch.inference_mode()
+    def test_graph_replay_matches_eager(self):
+        inputs = _inputs([2, 7])
+        eager_inputs = _clone_caches(inputs)
+        graph_inputs = _clone_caches(inputs)
+        expected = _fused(eager_inputs)
+        out = torch.empty_like(expected)
+        _fused(_clone_caches(inputs), out=out)
+        graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+        with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+            _fused(graph_inputs, out=out)
+        graph.replay()
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(out, expected))
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(graph_inputs["state"], eager_inputs["state"]))
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
